899.s: His birth on Bourbon Street in 1903; father Joseph and brother Joseph Jr. played trumpet, mother only sang.
899.q: She used to sing little songs and things around the house on white days and things, you know.

899.t: Euless Jean's background and the four-piece first band
899.s: Jean was born in New Orleans the same year, studied with his uncle Nelson Jean; Dollier cannot recall the rest of the four-piece band.
899.q: Yeah, he was born in New Orleans and he was raised, we was raised, he was raised on Ayquart Street and I was raised on Bourbon Street.

450.t: Birth in Surrey to Scottish vaudevillian parents
450.s: Ross gives her real name and says her parents were vaudevillians; the five children were brought on stage as babies and her one-legged father produced the act.
450.q: My real name is Annabelle McCauley Allan Short. My mother and father were vaudevillians in Scotland. They were on tour. I was born outside of London, in a place called Surrey. There was a tradition in our family – there were five of us in the family, three girls and two boys. As soon as we could…

450.t: Birthplace in Mitcham, Surrey, and the Metropolitan baby
450.s: At the interviewer's prompt she confirms Mitcham, Surrey, names the Judy Garland film, and tells how her mother performed through pregnancies and she was born after a matinee.
450.q: It’s – Surrey is a little town. Elton John was born there. That’s where I was born, in a house. It’s outside of London. That’s about it.

145.t: Born in Sapulpa; father's Texas band and move west
145.s: Royal confirms his birthdate and Sapulpa birthplace, and describes his parents from Texas, his father's reading band that tried out Scott Joplin scores, and the stopover in Oklahoma on the way to California.
145.q: My mother was born in Denison, Texas. My father was born in Sherman, Texas. My father was the leader of a orchestra. As a matter of fact, he was the leader of the first jazz band that ever came out of North Texas. It was the Marshal Royal Band. He played in the World's Fair in St. Louis, I believe,…

145.t: Father's birthdate and the St. Louis World's Fair
145.s: Pinning down his father's birth around 1881 and the fair as the 1904 Louisiana Purchase Exposition.
145.ch: Family follow-ups from the first reels
145.q: I know that the date had a four on the end of it. I didn't know whether it was '94 or 1904. But I'm pretty sure that it had a 4 on the end of it.

20.t: Born into a cornet-playing family uptown
20.s: Lee gives his birth date and streets; his father and grandfather played cornet and he started on his father's horn at six or seven.
20.q: Oh, it's going? Yeah. Hello, this is Lee Collins talking here. I was born in Deeroux, New Orleans, October 17, 1901. I was raised uptown. I'm almost born with a cornet. My daddy was a cornet player, my grandfather was a cornet player. They played with the old Tio boys, Lorenzo Tio's daddy and his…

402.t: Born in Mexico; Spanish parents and uncle Carlos Chavez
402.s: Sal says he was born near Jalisco, Mexico, of Spanish parents, on May 20, 1908, and that his mother's uncle was the composer Carlos Chavez.
402.q: Well, now I'll tell you, that's a long story, since you asked me a question. Yeah, okay. Now, truth is speaking, I don't believe in lying about nothing I'd say. So, you asked me kind of a sort of a first question. I said, no, as a matter of fact, I wasn't born here. I wasn't born, I wasn't born…

891.s: Born September 15, 1908 at Maroney and Johnson; only his brother fooled with a horn, no relatives played.
891.q: No, they're just arrows. Just put around this. You know, just one arrow here and one arrow. That was the time of Claude Gable suits come out. Well, they called them the Sheik. They used to have uptown pockets. You see, your pants was made like this, the pockets. They were a little more around in…

622.t: Born 1905, a lawyer and pianist, first jazz heard on records
622.s: Ashcraft gives his birth year, family and law career, and says he and the Austin boys first met jazz through records such as the Friars Inn Farewell Blues.
622.q: Well, I was born in 1905, which was approximately when most of the Austin High School band were born. I might add that I was probably born in just about the right place at about the right time for some unusual chances to observe, and I wish I'd observed a little better. Or at least I wish I'd…

249.t: Birth in 1894, Eighth Ward, and family
249.s: Born 24 March 1894 in the Eighth Ward; no musicians in the family except a cousin.
249.q: Outside of Franky Deuce was an off-cousin of mine. He's in his- He was a cousin, Franky Deuce.

253.t: Born in Reserve; father in the Onward Brass Band
253.s: Hall gives his birthplace and date (May 15, 1901), his musical family, and his father's clarinet in the Onward band, whose New York trip is dated 1892.
253.q: I was born in what's called Reserve Louisiana. Reserve Louisiana? Yeah, Reserve Louisiana. It's about what, about 20, 21 to 22 miles from here. And what date was that? That was May the 15th, 1901. Were any of your family musicals? Oh yeah, everybody's musical, whole musical family. My father was a…

871.t: Birth in the Creole part of New Orleans and musical family
871.s: Born 1899 on Villere Street in the French part of town; heard Dixieland; his uncle Emile Bigard played violin, brother Barney and cousin Natty Dominique played music.
871.q: I was born in the city of New Orleans, September 25th, 1899. In what part of town were you born? Do you remember? I mean, not as you remember, but where your folks live. In the French part of town, 1726 Northville, Creole part of town.

798.t: Birth, father Aaron Clark, and the warning against wind instruments
798.s: Clark gives his birth date and says his father, a musician, died months after he was born and told his mother never to let him play a wind instrument. He followed bands as a child anyway. Interviewers ask where his parents came from and where he was born.
798.q: My name is Joseph Clark. I was born February 12, 1894. My father's name is Aaron Warren Clark. He was born in 1876. He died September 14, 1894. He was a musician before I was born. And after I was born, before I was born, he'd taken sick. And he told my mother never to let me play a wind…

645.t: Birthplace on Tarragona Street and a musical family
645.s: Ida was born in Pensacola on Tarragona Street; her mother and father came from Florida towns and both played piano, as do her sisters.
645.q: Right here in Scola, Florida. I was born on the corner of 7th Avenue and, uh, no I wasn't, I was born on the 400 block on Tarragona Street during the time, uh, when they had that hotel down there for a couple of people years ago.

771.t: Birth in Algiers and musical family
771.s: Bocage gives his birthdate and says his father Paul played guitar in a small band; brothers Henry (bass) and Charlie (banjo) were also musicians.
771.q: Paul, Paul. Who did he play with, Peter? Well he played, he used to have a band, Old Man Dorset they call it years ago, they had, he didn't use over three or four pieces then, you know, violin, trumpet and guitar and bass, violin, you know. And how about your brothers, what were their names? Henry,…

241.t: Louis Nelson's birth and musical family
241.s: Nelson gives his 1902 birth and describes his pianist mother, doctor father and brother George.
241.q: Yes, my mother played. My father, he played all. So my mother, she was a graduate from the Boston Conservatory of Music. She was a pianist.

184.t: Born 1897 in Sellers, Louisiana; father Joseph Hall the brass band drummer
184.s: Hall gives his birth date and place, the move to New Orleans at about two, and his father's drumming in a country brass band.
184.q: Yeah, that's right. I think Papa Mutt, too, came from Hornsville. Yeah, I grew up in Hornsville. Yeah, so after all my mother and father, they moved from Yolens, I think I was about two years old, and I was practically raised in Yolens, and my brother, I don't know how he got started. See, my…

725.t: Birth in Algiers and the musical Bocage family
725.s: Born in Algiers in 1900; father, brothers, sisters and a cousin were musicians.
725.q: Well I had one sister named Boetha and uh, Lillian. And my father was uh, Leopold Vorkaige. And of course my other two brothers is uh, Henry and Boethaige, Henry Clay and uh, Peter Boethaige.

762.t: Birth in the old Quarter, parents and brother
762.s: Purnell gives his birth date and address, his father's drumming, his saxophonist brother, and the move to a Black neighborhood around age nine or ten.
762.q: I have one brother who is now a saxophone player. His name is Théodore Ponyo. I think he's been a little sick. But the last report I got from him that he was coming along real nicely. And I said we lived around this neighborhood until I imagine around 9, 10 years of age. And then my mother moved…

11.t: Birth, parents and father's accordion; first tries at piano
11.s: Born in 1894 in the French downtown part of New Orleans; father played accordion as a hobby; he tried piano before settling on clarinet.
11.q: I tried to play piano, but it didn't do good or wasn't successful. It seemed like my associates were the ones that I was visiting. Everyone was crazy about a clarinet, so I took a liking to it.

14.t: Birth in Blackman, Louisiana; musical parents and siblings
14.s: Love gives his birth date and place, says his father played cornet and mother cello, and that his father's band bought instruments by pooling money.
14.q: Alright Mr. Love can you tell us when you were born and just where? I was born in Blackman, Louisiana on October the 6th, 1885.

995.t: Birthplace in New Orleans and family origins
995.s: Born in New Orleans; mother from Mobile, grandmother from Santo Domingo; his father started him on drums.
995.q: Well, my mother come from Mobile, Alabama, but I wasn't sure where my father was from. But he had explained to me that my grandmother had come from St. Dominguez. Oh, yes. But he never did give me that town of Eastwood. What instrument you played for you, is the bandit or the piano? No, he stomped…

268.t: Born in Algiers, 1907; mother and relatives played music at home
268.s: Turner says he was born in Algiers in 1907. His mother, grandmother and aunt played piano at home but not professionally.
268.q: Well, my mother played in those pianos, the churches, you know. My grandmother, and I had an aunt, but she played in the church. But there wasn't a professional, you know. She played music. But, yeah, I'm going to say that.

271.s: Mello was born in 1887 near the interview house; no relatives were professional musicians, but his father played harmonica tunes like Swanee River.
271.q: Right here in the Walls, two blocks away from here, 1887. On Betholome? On Betholome in Ibogunny. And the exact date of your birth? June the 4th.

653.t: Birth date, his mother and his father's roots across the lake
653.s: Born September 5, 1934; his mother's Creole maiden name Jolivet; father's family came from Mandeville and Madisonville.
653.q: Well, as far as I know, most of my father's life was here, but he came from like across the river in Mandeville, Madisonville, around that area.

461.t: Born in Covington, 1902, and his parents' move there
461.s: Rene was born in Covington in 1902; his mother's tuberculosis moved the family there. His parents played piano and violin.
461.q: Well, I was born in Covington, Louisiana. My mother, my father was a contractor in New Orleans. And when my mother took sick with tuberculosis, they had to move to the ozone belt. That was Covington. Because of the pine trees and the good weather over there, that was best to get well. And so I was…

187.t: Birth in New Orleans, father the doctor, mother the pianist
187.s: Nelson gives his name and birthplace on Two Row Street, born 1902; father practiced medicine in Napoleonville; mother, a Boston Conservatory pianist, passed on the talent.
187.q: Well, when I was a baby about two months old, my daddy left me and he went out to a country town by the name of the family. He went out to a country town by the name of Napoleonville, Louisiana. And he practiced medicine out there. And we stayed out there for about 25 years or more. And I moved…

43.t: Born on Bourbon Street, 1895; mother's singing; catechism school
43.s: Lizzie was born in New Orleans on March 31, 1895. Her mother sang only late in life, and Lizzie began singing in catechism school since there was no money for lessons.
43.ch: Childhood and early career in New Orleans
43.q: My mother sings, but not publicly. Only until after she got in her old days, she started singing in old folks' concerts and singing old Creole songs, but when she was young, she didn't. She didn't? Mm-hmm.

44.t: Robert Pete Williams: nickname, Zachary birth 1914 and family
44.s: Pete Williams gives his nickname and birth in Zachary, Louisiana, in 1914; a sister and uncle play guitar.
44.q: Yes, sir. What instruments? Well, they play guitar. All of them? All of them play guitar. All of them play guitar. Well, pretty good things to the eyes. Mm-hmm. Yeah.

45.t: Birth in New Orleans and family without musicians
45.s: Williams was born September 1, 1900, in the Third Ward; he was an only child and no one in his family played music.
45.q: I was born in New Orleans, right here. What part of town? In the Third Ward, on Liberty between Lafayette and Padres. 1900 September 1st.

1008.t: Birth in Pensacola and the Morgan brothers
1008.s: Morgan was born in Florida in 1901 and raised in New Orleans; he lists brothers Sam, Robert, Isaiah and Albert.
1008.q: Well, I'm not the youngest brother, you see. Well, it was Sam. He was the oldest one. Then my brother Robert, he died. And I have another brother, Isaiah. And I came, a brother next to you, Isaiah. And come a brother, Albert, the bass player. He was much younger than the master. He was much younger…

631.t: Opening, birth, and a musical family
631.s: Interview opening in 1956; Loyacano gives his full name, 1889 birth on Magazine Street, siblings and the family instruments.
631.q: I wouldn't dare ask you this, but what's the date of your birth? Well, it's August 13th, 1889. Were you born in New Orleans? Born in New Orleans. What street, do you know? I was born on Magazine Street. Magazine in what? Near Thalia. And how many brothers and sisters did you have? Well, I had four…

279.t: Birth, and a grandfather who played French horn
279.s: Hug gives his birth date, and talks about his horn-playing grandfather's link to the Christian family.
279.q: Well Dick, I was born on Tulane Avenue, the exact address I don't know. I was born somewhere on Tulane. I was born December the 6th, 1910.

724.t: Birth in 1902, non-musical family and hearing clarinet at picnics
724.s: His parents and relatives did not play; he heard bands at picnics and wanted only to hear the clarinet.
724.q: Well, I had a brother who used to get a lot of picnics out of Millen Boyd. And Mount Perez. You know when Nelson used to play for him. Quite natural when they'd have things like that, they had to carry the children along. So, I'd be out there and listening at the music.

188.t: Birth, McCall plantation and musical family
188.s: Foster gives his name and birth date, says he grew up near Donaldsonville and left at 15 for New Orleans. His uncle and father played music and cousin Claiborne Williams led a top band.
188.q: Donaldsonville I went to school there up for his high school and I left when I was 15 years old and went to New Orleans during time I was there I learned how to play a mandolin a little violin

819.s: Sbarbaro says he was born June 27, 1897 near St. Claude and Rampart; nobody in his family played music.
819.q: Not one. Not even a kazoo? Not even a kazoo. Didn't sing or anything? No. I doubt a very few families out of New Orleans had a family musical background. Maybe the Detroit's and the Christians. Well, the Brunesses might have had one at that time. Oh, yeah. The old man played violin. Well, not my…

288.t: Born in Parks; father's baritone; the Parks band and dance jobs
288.s: Charles was born in 1891 in the house at Parks; his father played baritone in the Parks brass band and small dance units that toured nearby towns.
288.q: house was over there by the way i'm a garage here so just near the bayou and parks that's right i was born on april the eighteen nineteen hundred and i mean eighteen hundred and ninety one

681.t: Born in Greenville, Mississippi; father leads the Grand Opera House orchestra
681.s: Hirsch was born in Greenville; his father led the orchestra at the Grand Opera House, which hosted vaudeville, road shows and minstrel shows.
681.q: my father was a band, an orchestra leader. He was the orchestra leader at the Grand Opera House, which was a theater in Greenville, and he was the orchestra leader. And they used to have all kind of shows coming through there in those days. It was not an opera. Exactly as an opera, like La Tosca,…

1006.t: Born in New Orleans, raised in Bay St. Louis, father's band
1006.s: Alexis gives his birth (New Orleans, 1896), the family's move to Bay St. Louis, his father the violin professor, his drummer brother Joseph, and taking up cornet in his father's Dixieland band.
1006.q: You can just give your name then. My name is Rick Carter Lexus. I was born in New Orleans, Louisiana in 1896. You have the exact date? On the 16th date of October. And my mother and father moved from New Orleans and moved over to Basin Lewis, which my father was a professor of violin player, taught…

176.s: De De was born in New Orleans in 1904; no one in his family played music; they look at family photos.
176.q: Rushblaze, I don't know, market during the time. Rushblaze and, uh, Sudan. What? Orlinds and, uh, Orlinds, somewhere in that section anyway. Orlinds and Sudan somewhere, on Rushblaze 3. I see. I see. I see. I see.

193.t: Israel Gorman introduced: birth and family
193.s: Gorman is introduced after Butler could not recall his teacher; he was born in New Orleans and had a banjo-playing cousin.
193.q: i left algaes when i was nine years old i was born in new orleans that's where i raised him you have any music in your family or any neighbors who played well i had the cousin playing but he wasn't too much a player you know what i mean what was his name well his name was johnny john he died years…

781.t: Birth, New Orleans neighborhood and father Spencer Murray's band
781.s: Murray was born in 1896 near Eucousine Street; his father Spencer Murray played guitar and led his own band at Tom Anderson's, and his mother's family were country musicians in Livingston Parish.
781.q: I was born in 1896. Exact birthday? What month? 1896, October the night. 1325 South, no, 12-0. I'm going to get my house ready. You know how it is in conversation. I'm on 1225 Eucousine Street. Where is that? That's where the IC railroad track goes out. See, that's all been demolished now. Howard…

297.t: Birth in Port Island and his father the bass player
297.s: Summers was born September 15, 1903 across the river from Baton Rouge; his father L.M. Summers played string bass with several country bands.
297.q: 1903, September the 15th. Was that in New Orleans? No, in Port Island, Louisiana. Oh yeah. How far is that from here? About 190 miles from...cross the river. Cross the river from Baton Rouge.

909.t: Algiers birth, father, and Senator Brady's band
909.s: Born in Algiers; father worked in the Southern Pacific roundhouse. Earliest music was Senator Brady's band taught by Professor Humphrey in Wagamon, where Morris lived about 1910-12.
909.ch: Childhood and early music in Algiers
909.q: Senator Brady First had a band, you know And he put them all Had them all out The line music Professor Umford teach them Professor Umford teached the whole band He had about 12 or 15 pieces

766.s: He comes from the Nightwater section; a younger sister played piano.
766.q: Right in this section. Tramway. No, I come from Nightwater.

198.s: Barnes gives where he was born, then explains the serenade-style surprise party bands of violin, bass, guitar and clarinet, with no trombones.
198.ch: Blind Charlie, kin and early memories
198.q: Now, uh It used to be what you call a ceremony, you know, it was like a surprise party. Boy, it was all pride upon you, wait that night about nine, 10 o'clock, come with music in front of the door, a gang of people with your attention now. Before you break, then you know nothing about it.

25.t: Birth in Texarkana and mother's hymns
25.s: Taylor gives his birth place and date (January 1, 1894) and recalls his mother playing hymns on a foot organ and piano.
25.q: Well, the very first music I heard was about my mother. She used to play the organ, the old-fashioned foot organ, and later on we bought a flat-top piano. And I always heard my mother play the hymns from the church books. And that's, I got my inspiration from my mother, I guess.

303.t: Birth in Oakland, Mississippi, and his musical brothers
303.s: Born 1907; mother a concert pianist, father a country fiddler; brother Johnny with the Arcadian Serenaders, brother Dick the harmonica champion, then school and marriage.
303.q: You said your mother? Oh, yes. My mother was a concert pianist. My father played breakdown fiddle, hoedown fiddle, if you want to call it that. Country fiddle.

3.t: Born in Chattanooga; her father a musician
3.s: Austin says she was born in Chattanooga and her father was a musician and teacher in New York.
3.q: No, I was born in Chattanooga, Tennessee.

786.t: Shade's birth and his father the guitar maker
786.s: Shade was born in Memphis in 1898; his father made guitars, played blues and died before Shade knew him.
786.q: Ordered the parts. And sears and roll boys in different places. And put them together itself.

419.t: Growing up in Southern California's traditional jazz scene
419.s: Barrett was born in Pasadena, raised in Costa Mesa, and grew up around Sunday-afternoon Jazz Society meetings; he has played this festival three times.
419.q: Well actually I was born in this area, I’m originally from Southern California. I was born in Pasadena. I was about one year old when my parents moved to Costa Mesa in Orange County, and I grew up in the more traditional jazz scene, the Sunday afternoon Jazz Society meetings that are still held…

1011.t: No regrets; born in Attleboro and early musical exposure
1011.s: Conniff says he is fortunate to have done what he loves, was born in Attleboro in 1916, and was exposed to music by his parents; his dad taught him trombone at about nine.
1011.q: [coughs] pardon me. I hope there won’t be too much of that going on. I’ve got one of these California flu bugs or something. Oh, sure, you know, as we live life at the time, when we’re doing, like now what we’re doing, we think we’re doing the right thing for now. And I guess if you went back and…

209.t: Born in Milwaukee, family moves to California
209.s: Hardaway was born in Milwaukee and the family left when he was three; he jokes he couldn't find a rhythm section. He is nearly a native Californian.
209.q: We left when I was three years old, I couldn’t find a rhythm section.

961.t: Birthplace and growing up in Dallas and San Diego
961.s: Born in San Antonio but raised in Dallas, then San Diego from about age six during the war; moved to Los Angeles in the early 1960s and later back.
961.ch: San Diego and the state of jazz
961.q: No. We really lived in Dallas, my family. But we happened to — my father did a lot of traveling in his work and we were in San Antonio at that particular time for a brief time, I think just a few months. But really Dallas was where we lived. But then when I was about six, five or six we came out…

153.t: Birth name, birthdate and Rock Falls, Illinois
153.s: Bellson gives his full Italian birth name, explains the shortening to Bellson, and recounts being born 13 1/2 pounds in Rock Falls and the marked birthplace house. The family soon moved to Peoria and then Moline.
153.q: It was in the magazines for years. Leonard Feather had it 26 of July, but it’s really July 6th. I was born Luigi Paulino Alfredo Francesco Antonio Balassoni. With that I could [?] the cello and play it. But that’s my full name. The reason it was changed, because Dad had a music store at home.…

703.t: Birth in Los Angeles, raised in Pasadena
703.s: Born Robert Howard Hutcherson in Los Angeles in 1941 though the family lived in Pasadena; relatives helped at the birth.
703.q: No. It was – they were living in Pasadena, but a lot of my relatives were living in Los Angeles, Watts and stuff like that. So it worked out, because they could be there. My mom had me very late in her life, in those days, and so it was better for my father to take my mother to the Los Angeles…

368.t: Born in Camden, raised in South Philadelphia, and Philly's musicians
368.s: He gives his birth date and place, the move to Philadelphia, and names fellow Philadelphians Joe Wilder, Red Rodney and others.
368.q: I was born in Camden, New Jersey on Van Hook Street, I don’t know if it’s still there. And, but, shortly after, a few years, a couple years after that my family moved to Philadelphia. And I was kind of raised in south Philadelphia from that point on, until I left to go on the road.

526.t: Birth name, Swedish parents and moving to Oakland
526.s: She gives her birth name Lovella Mae Borg, her parents' names and Swedish background, and why the family ended up in Oakland.
526.q: Well, my full name is not the name I was born with. My real name that I was born with is, oh my god, I think I can say it. [Clears throat]. Lovella Mae Borg.

105.t: Birth date uncertainty and mixed-heritage family
105.s: Hamilton gives his name and says he was born in Los Angeles on September 21 or 23, 1921, and describes his mother's and father's mixed backgrounds.
105.q: Oh, I’m not going to tell you that, man. Okay, my name is Foreststorn Chico Hamilton, aka Chico Hamilton. I was born in LA in 1921, September the 21st or 23rd, 1921.

110.t: Birth at home in Concord, December 1920
110.s: He was born at home with Dr. Neff barely arriving in time, and his father was at the Keller ranch slaughterhouse.
110.ch: Family and boyhood in Concord and Ione
110.q: I was born at home. My mother realized that she was going to have a baby and went as fast as she could to Dr. Neff on [ ] a half a block away, and knocked on the door. I guess it was about four in the morning. Dr. Neff came to the door and said, “Bessie, go home and get in bed, and I’ll be right…

86.t: Birth in Kentucky, raised in Columbus; uncle teaches him trumpet scales
86.s: He gives his birth year, says his parents separated when he was six months old, and recalls the blues records in Kentucky and the uncle who taught him scales.
86.q: Actually I was born in Kentucky, Beaverdam, Kentucky, but my mom and pop, they separated when I was six months old and she took me to Columbus, OH. At six months old you don’t know where you are, so I just adopted Columbus, OH as my home because I’ve been there all my life, finished school there…

116.s: Marsalis gives his birth, his parents' origins and his father's motel business in Jefferson Parish.
116.q: No, not exactly. Let’s see. I think my father when he was, I think, about 13, because my grandfather – his father – he worked on the L&N Railroad as a fireman. I’m not sure when my mother came, because she came from New Roads to New Orleans, but the year, I don’t know. They didn’t talk a lot about…

527.t: Birth in Council Bluffs, twin brother Addison, parents
527.s: Interview opening, then Farmer gives his name, birth in Council Bluffs, Iowa, twin brother Addison, and his parents' names and siblings.
527.q: Addison, yes well, we were twin brothers. I was born one hour in front of him, and he was larger than me, a bit. And we were very close.

107.t: Birth, parents and Cincinnati as a musical crossroads
107.s: Foster gives his birth details and his parents' South Carolina origins, then describes segregated, culturally mixed Cincinnati and the big bands that played the Coliseum.
107.q: I was born Frank Benjamin Foster the Third at 2:15 a.m., September 23rd, 1928, to Lillian Watts Foster and Frank B. Foster. My mother’s maiden name was Lillian Iona Watts. My mother and father were natives of South Carolina, my father from Greenville and my mother from Seneca. My father came north…

491.t: Name, birth date, parents and being an only child
491.s: Golson gives his name, Philadelphia birth and date, discusses discrepant birthdates, the spelling of his name, his parents' Southern origins and meeting in a church choir, and having no siblings.
491.q: My mother was Celadia – C-e- l-a-d-i-a – York. She was from Mobile, Alabama. My father was Benny Golson. He spelled his name B-e-n-n-i-e. However, I changed mine to a “y,” legally.

371.t: Father's lifelong job with General Motors; birth in Vicksburg
371.s: His father worked for the companies that became General Motors; Jones was born in Vicksburg, not Pontiac.
371.ch: Pontiac childhood, family and piano training
371.q: He worked for General Motors for all of his life. At first the company was called Bodett Brothers, then it was called Fishbodies, then it was called Yellow Truck and Coach, then it was called General Motors. You see, General Motors absorbed all of these other companies. But, he worked there all of…

224.t: Birth, parents from Barbados and siblings
224.s: Haynes gives his birth, his parents' names and Barbadian origin, and his three brothers.
224.q: Douglas Haynes. That was the oldest brother. Vincent Haynes. Douglas was born in Barbados. Vincent Haynes was born in Boston. Roy Haynes, Boston. Michael Haynes, Boston. He’s the youngest.

135.t: Birth, parents and the Heath siblings' nicknames
135.s: Heath gives his full name, birth in Wilmington, NC in 1923, his parents, and his sister Elizabeth and brothers Jimmy and Tootie, whom their grandfather nicknamed.
135.q: Well, we had a sister, Elizabeth. She wanted to be called Betty, but we called her Lizzy all her life. And my grandfather on my mother’s side gave us all nicknames. And she was Lizzy, Tin Lizzy, like the old automobile. I was Percolator. And Jimmy, I think he called Jimmy, Shorty, which I don’t…

111.t: Born in Pontiac as a twin; parents from Vicksburg
111.s: Elvin was born in 1927, his twin Elvin Roy died at six months, and his parents Henry and Olivia came from Vicksburg, Mississippi.
111.q: Elvin Jones: My name is Elvin Ray Jones. I was born in Pontiac, Michigan in 1927; as one half of a twin, I was a twin! (chuckles). And my twin brother, we both had whooping cough, and he didn’t survive longer than 6 months. You know, I can remember the funeral and everything. Cause I used to tell…

953.t: Birth in Harlem, parents and grandparents from the Danish Virgin Islands
953.s: Rollins gives his birth name and date, his parents' names and origins in St. Croix and St. Thomas, and what he knew of his grandparents.
953.q: Oh, I was afraid you were going to ask me that. Ok, my full name at birth was Walter Theodore Rollins, and I was born September 7, Sunday morning, 1930 in Harlem, America uh on 137th Street between Lenox and 7th Avenues. Uh, there was a midwife that delivered me, and that was my–how I entered into…

509.t: Birth, parents and her two brothers
509.s: Horn gives her birthplace, her parents' names and origins, and her two brothers, neither a musician.
509.q: My mother‘s a native Washingtonian. My father is from East St. Louis. My mother‘s from Ivy City, Northeast, which is not too far from where we are now, Ivy City.

64.t: Born in Greenville, North Carolina; moves to Raleigh and Washington
64.s: Taylor gives his name, birth in 1921, his parents' meeting at Howard, and the family's moves from Greenville to Raleigh and back to Washington.
64.q: Well my name is William Edward Taylor Junior. I am named after my father. When someone said William in my family in Washington D.C. or in North Carolina almost everybody head in the room turned. We had more Williams…it was the favorite family name I guess. So I am a junior. I was born in…

136.t: Her parents, her three older sisters and her father's work in Manchuria
136.s: She names her parents, their Kyushu origins, her birth date and her father's textile job and later trading company.
136.q: My father‟s name is Katsurō Akiyoshi. My mother‟s maiden name is Hiraike, so her name is Shigeko Hiraike. And they were married, I don‟t know when, wherever, [laughs] and when I was born, I‟m the last of the four daughters. Four daughters.

528.s: Tyner gives his birth name and date, his parents' North Carolina roots, his father's job and his brother Jarvis and sister Gwen.
528.q: My father worked in a company that made medicated cream. As a matter of fact, I got a job there. His boss got to know me and my father said, “Ah, let him come in on Saturday.” And then I was putting the medication stuff in the jars (laughs) with the machine, it was nice, an actual job. I could go…

553.t: Birth as William Huddleston and moves to Detroit
553.s: Lateef gives his birth name, birthplace Chattanooga, moves to Lorain and Detroit, and the family name change to Evans.
553.q: Well, my full name now is Yusef Abdul Lateef; however, I was born uh my name was William Emanuel Huddleston. I was born October 9, 1920 in Chattanooga, Tennessee.

80.t: How his parents met; half-siblings; birth in 1904
80.s: Von jokes it was a secret; Autrey explains his mother had four children before marrying his father, a baseball player and musician, and that he was born December 4, 1904.
80.ch: Boyhood in Evergreen and Calhoun school
80.q: Yes, my father was introduced to my mother by a good friend of hers and a neighbor of ours who lived next door, and Von just reminded me that my father played baseball. He was a very good baseball player, and a good musician, which he and worked, played together in the same band, you know, in the…

406.t: Birth, parents and the coal town of Scandia near Des Moines
406.s: Barefield was born 12 December 1909; his father, a coal miner, sang blues and played guitar, his mother took piano lessons. The family had records, and Scandia has since been absorbed by Des Moines, where he went to school until about 16.
406.ch: Des Moines childhood and first bands
406.q: Oh, yes. I have about six people in my family who are Sagittarians. My brother, my sister and I, my brother, we're all born in December. And I have a grandson who was born on the same day I was born.

113.t: Birth in Muskogee and growing up with three sisters
113.s: McShann gives his birth date, January 12, 1916, and says he was the only boy among four children, outnumbered by his three older sisters.
113.q: Oh, I don't think so because -- well, you know, you take three girls and a mother in a home, there's no chance for -- even being the youngest boy, to get spoiled

614.t: Birth date, records and radio at home
614.s: Born May 16, 1913, in Milwaukee. He bought his own records and listened to dance bands on an Atwater Kent radio in his room.
614.q: Some, but not a great deal. Actually, the earliest records I bought on my own and got some sort of phonograph. But radio was just coming in very strong, and that was influencing all of us. And so I had, I guess, one of the early Atwater Kents in my room, and I was able to listen to music and bands…

26.t: Birth in Long Branch and family background
26.s: Greer gives his birth date and place, his parents' work and his siblings, and says nobody in his family was musical.
26.q: My family background. I can remember all of my family. My mother's name was Elizabeth. My father's name was William Alexander. I was named after him but they always called me from the time I remember Son. They would say Son, and then they changed it to Sonny. My mother was a modiste and my father…

87.t: Musicians who came out of Savannah and Georgia
87.s: James Moody came from Savannah and Higginbotham from Atlanta; Young left Savannah in 1926 at 14.
87.q: Later years but I didn't know him them. James Moody came out of Savannah. But I didn't know Moody at that particular time. I guess there are other guys who I really don't know who were musicians in Savannah that came out. There were good musicians all through the South, Atlanta and Savannah.…

677.t: Birth date, Lawrence Kansas and his minister father
677.s: Brown corrects his birth date to August 3, 1907, says he was born in Lawrence, Kansas, to an A.M.E. minister, was likely named for Paul Laurence Dunbar, and recalls his mother playing organ in Fort Scott.
677.q: Well, there have been several errors from time to time. I guess I gave out the wrong information from time to time, but my real birth date is August the 3rd, 1907. That's in the Chilton book.

4.t: Birth in Dallas, siblings and parents
4.s: Spikes was born in Dallas on October 31, 1888, the youngest of five living children; he names his brothers, sisters, mother Medora Kirby and father Munroe.
4.q: Richard and Johnny, and I had a...well, a half-brother named Tom, the oldest one, and my sisters were named Viola and Annie.

67.t: Birth near Nashville and the nickname Doc
67.s: Cheatham was born in 1905 outside Nashville and got the name Doc from the medical-college neighbourhood; he played cornet in a little symphony, later soprano sax.
67.q: Born in Nashville, Tennessee. June 13, 1905. In fact it was outside of Nashville, in a little town between Nashville and Murfreesboro, but now it's called all the city of Nashville.

9.t: Birth in Boston and the Holmes family of siblings
9.s: Holmes gives his birth date and place and names his brothers and sisters; the family was large, with up to thirteen children over time.
9.ch: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
9.q: I should think that they would know. Okay. My name is Charlie Holmes, born January 27, 1910. Mmm! Boston, Massachusetts. Seven o'clock in the evening -- so they tell me. Now, you've got to ask me some questions.

106.t: Born in Charleston in 1901; parents from Mississippi
106.s: Briggs gives his birth date and place, his parents' origins, his father's work as sanitary inspector and preacher, and his place as the youngest of eleven children.
106.ch: Charleston childhood and the Jenkins Orphanage
106.q: Yes, Charleston was a, pretty -- yes, pretty well known, more or less,-- quite a lot of poverty and naturally--- but it was prospering, how do you say, prospering, yes.

68.t: Birth in Sherman, Texas, and his farmer father
68.s: Tate gives his birth date and place, his parents' origins, his father's three farms and early death, and being raised by older siblings.
68.q: Well, I think they all are from -- my mother was -- I think she was raised in Oklahoma, but on my dad's side, they're all from Texas, a little town that's called Polly Grove , Texas, a small place. It's between Dallas and Sherman.

166.t: Birth in Haskell and first memory of a band in Muskogee
166.s: Simmons gives his birth date and place, and recalls Everett Jackson, a sousaphone player, as his first memory of a band.
166.ch: Childhood in Oklahoma, Kansas City and Tulsa
166.q: I was on the farm three years, and I left there and went to Muskogee, Oklahoma. And my first memory of a band was Everett Jackson, who was a sousaphone bass player, and the reason that I can remember it so well, by this wrapping around his head, I thought he was being tortured.

28.t: Born in Foggy Bottom, mother's Louisiana family, absent father
28.s: Butler was born in Washington in 1909 in Foggy Bottom; his mother was from Lafayette, Louisiana (Lefebvre family, Negro and Indian mix) and he never really knew his father.
28.q: Well, I was born in Washington. The District of Columbia, it was called, in 1909. I was born in an area called Foggy Bottom. It was called Foggy Bottom because when they built Lincoln's tomb, they forgot -- neglected so that frogs (inaudible) and it seems that the river would overflow, you'd have…

380.t: Birth near Richmond, Virginia, and a catfish childhood
380.s: Callender describes his conception in Boston, birth in Virginia, move to Atlantic City, and confirms his birth date and the family farm at Haynesville where he fished with his grandfather.
380.q: ....[FIRST MINUTE NOT AUDIBLE]... For some reason, my mother went to Boston to work, I think, during that time, for a private family or something. And my father was a steward on a ship at that time. And they met. And so, I was conceived in Boston, but afterwards they married, of course -- they had…

90.t: Birth in Jackson and his father the multi-instrumentalist
90.s: Edwards gives his birth date and place; his father played trombone and other instruments and read music superbly but left Jackson before he was born.
90.q: Right. One is incorrect. They corrected it later. That was taken from an album I did on Pacific Jazz, where the guy that did the liner notes had the wrong date, and that one seemed to have got into more print than the rest of them!

69.t: Birth in San Juan, sister and parents
69.s: Tizol confirms he was born January 22, 1900 in San Juan, and names his sister Remedio and his parents Juan Tizol and Manuela Martinez.
69.q: Oh yes. Most certainly, they had been there for a long time, but there are quite a few that are dead now, you know.

70.t: Born in Springfield, Ohio; parents and two sisters
70.s: Jackson gives his birth date, his parents' names and the names and birth years of his two sisters; he is the middle child.
70.ch: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
70.q: Marguerite was -- my older sister, rather, was born in 1903. I was born in '09 and Marguerite was born in '17.

452.t: Born in Houston in 1918; a musical family
452.s: Cobb gives his birth date, August 10, 1918, and says his grandmother taught piano and his mother, an uncle and an aunt played.
452.q: I was born in Houston, Texas in the year of 1918, August 10. And that gives a little indication of my age, when you said 1978. It makes me 59 now, until August 10th.

232.t: Birth in Nacogdoches, move to Taft, and being named Ernie Lawrence Fields
232.s: Fields gives his birth date, parents, his father's death in 1906, and how he went by Sonny Boy until he named himself.
232.q: I was born in Nacogdoches, Texas, Sunday at midnight, August 28, 1904. Reverend Thomas Jefferson Fields was my father and Mary Jane Garrett Fields, mother. The baby of the family of three boys and two girls. The family moved to an all black town, Taft, Oklahoma, 1905. At that time, indian territory.

234.t: The newspaper article by J. C. Thomas about Gil
234.s: Johnston mentions a journalist's article about Gil. Anita reads its opening lines about his 1912 birth and step-father's name.
234.q: The New York, The Herald, it was a paper around for a while. I don't know if it still exists. A Sunday, every Sunday or maybe even every other.

71.t: Born in Parsons, Kansas, and his musical parents
71.s: Clayton gives his birth date and place, says he studied piano from age six, and describes his father (cornet, later a minister) and mother (piano, beauty parlour).
71.q: Yes. I was born in Parsons, Kansas. It's a small town in South East Kansas about 150 miles from Kansas City, Missouri. I was born November 12, 1911. And I went to school there and I began my first musical studies when I was six years old. I was learning piano and I studied piano until I was 18…

18.t: Born on a farm: twin brother and his name
18.s: He was the youngest of 14 children and a twin; his twin C. B. died at six months, and he changed Charlie to Jay C.
18.ch: Family, Margaret's story and Eutris's memories
18.q: I wasn't tell you - yes, I will. It was Charlie (Bronica.) Mine was just Charlie but I changed it to Jay C.

72.t: Little Washington and nearby North Carolina towns
72.s: He explains the town name and lists nearby North Carolina cities.
72.q: Well, Little Washington, North Carolina... The reason why they called it Little Washington was to put the... There's a distinction between Little Washington and Washington, North Carolina...Washington, D.C., rather... I always heard that Little Washington wasn't on the map. So I learned later it is…

73.t: A year in Charleston; his son is born
73.s: He stayed a year or more, helped his father-in-law the contractor, and his first son was born.
73.q: And I used to help him quite a bit doing odd jobs and what-not, you know.

31.t: Birth in Boston, Everett childhood and his parents
31.s: Whaley was born in Boston in 1892 and raised in Everett; he recalls a burglary scare, names his parents, and describes his father's Virginia family and supposed Indian ancestry.
31.ch: Early life and training in Boston
31.q: I was born in Boston at the corner of Church and Melrose in 1892. And my father and mother moved to Boston after six months of living there, I mean to Everett, Massachusetts. It's about six or seven miles from Boston, just like from New York to Brooklyn. And well, the first thing I remember was in…

237.t: Birth in Pineville and the Star Theatre job in Shreveport
237.s: Lovett says he was born in Pineville, moved to Alexandria then Shreveport, and spent about eight years in a theatre band there before coming to Kansas City.
237.q: Well, I was born in Pineville, Louisiana and I came to Alexandria, Louisiana when I was a very, very young man. And I moved from Alexandria, Louisiana to Shreveport, Louisiana, and I had a job in Shreveport at the Star Theatre, Texas Avenue. And I was there for I guess about eight years all…

124.t: Born in Philadelphia; the McRae family and brothers
124.s: McRae gives his name, says he was born in Philadelphia in 1908, and names his brothers and sister; his father was a real estate man.
124.ch: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
124.q: : Well, my full name was not my stage -- I'll say this. My name is Theodore McRae, "M-c-R-a-e. My stage name is Teddy, T-e-d-d-y M-c-R-a-e. Is that capital R? Capital R, yes. I was born in Philadelphia in 1908. My family is from Atlanta. They moved some time ago, and I was practically raised in…

7.t: Born in Muskogee, Oklahoma, 1907; parents and siblings
7.s: Thomas gives his birth date, the Oklahoma statehood land giveaway, his siblings George and Cleora born in Texas, and his parents' names and origins.
7.q: I was born February the Tenth, 1907. And to put it in the right perspective, I was born a month and teen days after Oklahoma went into statehood.

455.t: Born in Dallas; brother saves him from a house fire
455.s: Born December 14, 1910; his four-year-old brother got him out of a burning house when he was two.
455.q: I was born in Dallas, Texas, December 14th, 1910. You know, a funny thing, it isn't funny, my parents were out one night to some friends' and they left me and my brother at home. My brother was playing around with some matches, and the house caught on fire. And he had just -- he was four years old,…

103.t: Birth in Chicago and his father's travelling work
103.s: Jones gives his birth date (October 7, 1911), his parents' names, and says his father, a government artificer, was shifted around the country.
103.q: At that precise time I would not and I could not possibly know; because of the nature of my father's work, which I wasn't any too familiar with, he was being shifted around in various parts of the United States and to my recollection -

112.t: Born in Philadelphia in 1895; father the Biddles' butler
112.s: Wooding gives his birth date and Rodman Street home and describes his father's work as butler and steward for the Biddle family.
112.q: Well, Chris, I was born in Philadelphia. June 17, 1895. Well, at that time, most of the black people lived in South Philadelphia, so where we have -- my father was lucky enough to have his own home, it was rather small. But all three of, our four children, were born at 1119 Rodman St., where we…
